title: Bubbling Moon round 2: Miss Clou, the helmeted cat and its trolley, Pip crawling, Pip's rocket
prompt:
THE WORLD: the Bubbling Moon, a strange, silly and slightly sad moon in a children's game (never scary). Its milk lakes have dried into cracked, glossy white crust that mirrors the sky. Giant cheese craters full of Swiss-cheese holes are the pits. Bubbles of old milk pop up out of the ground on a slow beat, as if the moon had hiccups. A big wobbling curd drifts across the dry lake like a slow boat. The cats built an old, half-finished, high-tech milk pumping station here: steel grey with orange and yellow trim, rust, paw-print logos and coloured cables. Palette: milk white, cream, butter yellow, cheese orange, pale lavender and blue-grey shadows, a deep violet night sky.

MISS CLOU (use exactly this design): an orange tabby she-cat with big green eyes and a calm, sharp, slightly smug face, a dark brown nose, pointed ears, a long fluffy orange tail. She wears a white space suit with orange and dark-grey trim, black gloves and boots, dark knee and elbow pads, a dark tool belt, a small round glowing CYAN gauge in the middle of the chest, and a round clear glass bubble helmet over her ears. On her back a compact white and orange life-support pack with two small ion boosters (a little cyan flame when they fire). NOT a dark blue suit, NO cape. About 52 art pixels tall standing, a little taller than Pip.

You are drawing a SPRITE SHEET for the Bubbling Moon level of a side-view platformer. Everything is seen strictly from the side (a 2D platformer; not isometric, not top-down).

FORMAT
- One PNG, 3840 x 2160, landscape. Background: ONE flat, solid, bright pure green (#00FF00) everywhere behind the items. No checkerboard, no scenery, no ground strip, no frames or boxes round items, no title, no legend. No bright green inside the items (the green eyes of Miss Clou and any mould are a darker, duller green).
- Follow the row plan below, rows from top to bottom, items from left to right, exactly the items listed (one drawing each, nothing extra, nothing missing; the frames of one animation are the same size, side by side, on the same ground line, identical in colours and proportions). Items stand on a common ground line in their row. Leave at least 6 art pixels (24 image pixels) of empty green all round every item; no item may touch another item or the edge.
- Under each item a short label in small plain white text (catalogue style) with a clear gap between the label and the item above it and the tops of the items in the row below. The label is the item's name exactly as given in quotes. Keep the labels short.

STYLE (a program cuts this picture into pixel-art sprites for a game, so follow it exactly)
- TRUE 16-bit (Super Nintendo style) pixel art on a strict fixed grid: every art pixel is a perfectly square, evenly coloured 4 x 4 block of image pixels, so every pixel can be counted by eye. Edges of shapes are clean staircases of whole square pixels: never smooth curves, never soft or noisy shading, never JPEG-like speckle, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no blur, no glow halos, no dithering noise, no drop shadows, no cast shadows on the ground. Each shade is ONE exact flat colour; use only a small palette of about 32 colours for the whole picture, the same colour every time it is used.
- A clean, continuous, dark near-black-brown (#1A1410) outline exactly 1 art pixel (4 image pixels) thick round EVERY item (except where a line says "no outline", for soft things), also round white, cream and pale items so they stand out from the green; used ONLY for outlines. No fill colour darker than #40382F. Inside the outline shade each material with 2 or 3 flat tones and a few hard-edged pixel highlights, like the references.
- Match the three attached reference pictures in pixel size, line weight, saturation and level of detail: (1) the game's own props sheet (its green ground is the ground to use here too); (2) a finished sheet of this level's pumping-station props: match its pixel size, line weight, colours and shading exactly; (3) the hero, Pip the mouse astronaut: he is 49 art pixels tall, which fixes the scale of everything.
- SCALE: Pip is 49 art pixels (196 image pixels) tall; everything is drawn at that same pixel size. Sizes below are in art pixels (width x height), only roughly.
- Glass, bubbles and windows are drawn in opaque pale colours with a white highlight: nothing is see-through, and nothing is drawn behind an item.
- No text inside the items except where a line gives the words. Seen strictly from the side (a 2D platformer), light from the upper left.

ROW PLAN (5 rows)
Row 1, MISS CLOU, side view facing RIGHT (the design above) (every item in this row belongs to the group "missclou"), 5 items: 1 "stand" standing calmly, arms by her sides, a slight smug smile, tail curled behind; 2 "cool" arms folded across her chest, one eyebrow raised, smug and mysterious, weight on one leg; 3 "startled" startled: ears flat back, eyes wide, both arms up, tail puffed up, one foot lifted; 4 "hover-1" hovering a little above the ground on her boosters, a small cyan flame under the pack, legs dangling, arms folded; 5 "hover-2" the same hover, the cyan flame flickering a different shape.
Row 2, MISS CLOU IN THE BOX (a plain brown cardboard box with a cat paw stamp, front view, about 46 x 30; she has NO helmet in the box) (every item in this row belongs to the group "missclou"), 2 items: 1 "box-open-cat" the open box with Miss Clou's orange tabby head and her two paws over the rim, ears flat, green eyes narrowed in a deep glare, grumpy and sulking; 2 "box-closed-cat" the box with its flaps folded shut over her, only two narrowed glaring green eyes in a slit and her orange tail hanging over the side.
Row 3, THE HELMETED CAT (a big grey tabby cat in a bulky metal mind-control helmet: a grey dome with a small antenna on top and a blinking red light in front, glazed sleepy eyes; a victim, not a monster) (every item in this row belongs to the group "cat"), 5 items: 1 "trolley" an empty low steel pump trolley: a flat cart with four wheels, a handle and a small pump nozzle, paw logo (80 x 36); 2 "helmet-asleep-1" the grey cat curled up asleep on the trolley, the helmet on, the red light ON (80 x 50); 3 "helmet-asleep-2" the same, breathing in: the body a little higher, the red light dim (80 x 52); 4 "helmet" the helmet alone on the ground, its dome cracked open in two halves, the red light dead (30 x 24); 5 "freed" the same grey cat without the helmet, sitting up, plain surprised eyes wide, ears up (40 x 44).
Row 4, PIP CRAWLING (Pip the mouse astronaut from the third reference picture: the same orange mouse, big pink ears, round glass helmet, white suit, red scarf, tank; side view facing RIGHT, on hands and knees, about 36 art pixels long and 30 tall) (every item in this row belongs to the group "pip"), 6 items: 1 "crawl-1" crawl cycle frame 1: left hand and right knee forward; 2 "crawl-2" frame 2: passing; 3 "crawl-3" frame 3: right hand and left knee forward; 4 "crawl-4" frame 4: passing; 5 "pop-out-1" popping out of a hole: arms up and stretched forward, head high, mid-leap, 40 x 46; 6 "pop-out-2" landing from the pop: crouched, arms down, 40 x 36.
Row 5, PIP'S BOTTLE ROCKET (a home-made rocket: a clear plastic bottle as the body, a tin can as the cockpit, three little mismatched rocket motors at the back, loose wires and lots of silver duct tape, a wobbly fin; side view pointing RIGHT, about 120 x 56) (every item in this row belongs to the group "ending"), 5 items: 1 "rocket" the rocket as it is; 2 "rocket-tank" the same rocket with a squat steel canister (a pump housing with a ring of bolts and an orange band) bolted under the bottle as a fuel tank; 3 "bolt-1" the canister held in the air just under the bottle, unbolted; 4 "bolt-2" the canister against the bottle, two bolts in; 5 "bolt-3" the canister bolted on, a wrench resting on it.
